avis.titre: A Simple, Affordable Night Cream That Actually Works
avis.texte: Let me just say this upfront: you do not need a $98 cream in a fancy jar to have soft, glowing, younger-looking skin. I’m 54, my skin is dry, and I get asked if I’m in my 30s on the regular. This CeraVe Night Cream is a big part of why. I know it’s technically marketed for nighttime, but my skin is Sahara-level dry, so I use it during the day too. I layer a tiny bit of castor oil underneath (an aesthetician recommended that combo to me), and my face stays moisturized, calm, and honestly as soft as a baby’s bottom. What I Love: • Deep hydration without feeling greasy It’s thick in the jar but melts right into your skin — perfect under makeup or on its own. • Gentle, no-fragrance formula My skin is sensitive, and this doesn’t irritate or break me out at all. • Peptides + ceramides + hyaluronic acid Basically all the things every expensive brand brags about… except this one is actually affordable. • Skin looks smoother and more rested After a few weeks, my fine lines looked less noticeable and my skin barrier felt stronger. A quick heads up: It doesn’t come with an inner seal inside the jar — that’s normal for this product, but good to mention for anyone wondering. Bottom Line: This is one of the best moisturizers you can buy at this price point. If you have dry or mature skin, skip the pricey stuff and try this first. Your skin (and your wallet) will thank you.

avis.texte: I’ve been genuinely impressed with this night cream. I’ll admit — I used to believe that higher price automatically meant better results. avis.texte: I've been using CeraVe Skin Renewing Night Cream for a while now, and overall I'm very happy with it. I have psoriasis, so finding a moisturizer that actually helps without irritating my skin can be difficult. Many lotions and creams I've tried in the past cause a burning or stinging sensation when I first apply them, especially on areas where my skin is dry or irritated. This night cream does not do that at all. The cream feels rich and nourishing, but it absorbs well and doesn't leave my skin feeling greasy. It helps keep my skin soft, smooth, and hydrated throughout the night, and I've noticed that my skin feels much more comfortable and less tight by morning. The combination of ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and peptides seems to work very well for maintaining moisture and supporting my skin barrier. The only reason I'm giving it 4 stars instead of 5 is because the jar was much smaller than I expected. I was surprised by the size when it arrived, especially considering the price. Since I use moisturizer regularly due to my psoriasis, I know I'll go through it fairly quickly. Despite the smaller size, I would still recommend this product to anyone looking for a gentle, moisturizing night cream, especially those with sensitive or dry skin. The fact that it keeps my skin soft and doesn't burn when applied makes it stand out from many other moisturizers I've tried.

avis.texte: I really like this CeraVe Skin Renewing Night Cream. I’ve been using it every night for months, and it has become an essential part of my bedtime routine. avis.titre: Made Me Break Out All Over

Now that I'm older I still have the occasional pimple, but nothing terrible since I use a salicylic acid cleanser every morning. I also started using Niacinamide, which made my face even less red and acne non-existent for the past month! However, I also started using a retinol cream which dried out my skin a bit, so I tried this night cream because it had just great reviews, is labeled non-comedogenic, etc. My acne is now as bad as it was when I was in middle school! I'm broke out across my chin, the bridge of my nose, neck, and chest. I haven't had acne on my neck or chest since puberty. If I had used it longer it might've moisturized my skin, and the scent isn't bad. But if you have sensitive or acne-prone skin, just be careful. This had cetyl alcohol in it (which is what makes it so thick and creamy). Normally this isn't a bad thing, but I've now read this can cause sensitive skin to break out. Apparently it's best to stick to thin or light moisturizers if you have these skin conditions, which I'm definitely now doing!
